summary: This article covers the life and work of Al-Jazari, an engineer who built water pumps, an elephant clock, and moving automata about 800 years ago and wrote a famous book of machines.
introduce: Ask students why someone might write “Al-Jazari: Inventor of Machines”: to inform, to persuade, or to entertain? Take a quick hand vote, then tell students to look for clues about the writer's purpose as they read.

keyTerms.def: a person who uses science and math to plan and build machines, roads, or buildings
to plan how something will look and work before it is made
a part that opens and closes to control how much liquid or gas flows through a pipe

challengeTerms.def: a book or document written by hand, especially before printing was common
a bent arm on a wheel or rod that changes turning motion into back-and-forth motion, or the other way around

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that inventors from long ago still shape the machines we use today? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how Al-Jazari's machines made life easier or more interesting for people.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review engineer, design, and valve, and let weak readers underline sentences that inform and circle any that persuade.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use ingenious, manuscript, and crank in a short paragraph that explains the writer's purpose and how the details support it.
